Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.4","number":"13.4","heading":"Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14","number":"14","heading":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.1","number":"14.1","heading":"As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.2","number":"14.2","heading":"Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. To the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Feedback is voluntary; Vendor may use generalized suggestions without identifying Customer or disclosing Customer Confidential Information, and Customer retains the unrestricted right to use its own feedback.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15","number":"15","heading":"CUSTOMER DATA AND PRIVACY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.1","number":"15.1","heading":"Vendor shall process Customer Data only on Customer's documented instructions, to provide the Services, and as permitted by this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data, use it for advertising, combine it with another customer's identifiable data, or train a generally available model on it without Customer's express written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-15.2","number":"15.2","heading":"Each Party shall comply with Applicable Law concerning personal information. If Vendor processes personal information for Customer, the Parties' data-processing addendum is incorporated. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. At minimum, Vendor shall implement least-privilege access, multifactor authentication, encryption in transit and at rest, secure development, vulnerability management, logging, backup, business continuity, and annual workforce training.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.2","number":"17.2","heading":"Vendor shall notify Customer without undue delay and no later than twenty-four hours after confirming unauthorized access to, acquisition, disclosure, alteration, loss, or destruction of Customer Data or a material compromise of systems used to provide the Services (a “Security Incident”). Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. On request, Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance and evidence of relevant coverage. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.4","number":"19.4","heading":"For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20","number":"20","heading":"INDEMNIFICATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.1","number":"20.1","heading":"Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.2","number":"20.2","heading":"Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.3","number":"20.3","heading":"Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.4","number":"20.4","heading":"The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. The indemnifying Party may not settle a claim by admitting fault of, imposing non-monetary obligations on, or failing to fully release the indemnified Party without prior written consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.5","number":"20.5","heading":"For an infringement claim, Vendor shall, at its expense and in addition to its defence obligations, procure continued use, modify or replace the affected item without materially reducing functionality, or, if neither is commercially reasonable, terminate the item and refund prepaid and implementation Fees on a straight-line three-year basis. Vendor may not terminate unaffected Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21","number":"21","heading":"LIMITATION OF LIABILITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.1","number":"21.1","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.2","number":"21.2","heading":"Except for Excluded Claims, neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill, to the extent those damages are legally excludable. Costs of restoring Customer Data, obtaining replacement services, required notices, and reasonable incident response are direct damages.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.3","number":"21.3","heading":"“Excluded Claims” means a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations; its indemnification obligations; gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud; or infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property. Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-21.4","number":"21.4","heading":"The limitations allocate risk between sophisticated Parties and apply only to the maximum extent permitted by Applicable Law. Nothing limits liability that cannot lawfully be limited. Each cap and exclusion is independent and survives failure of an exclusive remedy.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22","number":"22","heading":"AUDIT RIGHTS","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.1","number":"22.1","heading":"Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.2","number":"22.2","heading":"Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-22.3","number":"22.3","heading":"Audit findings are Customer Confidential Information and may be used only to enforce this Agreement. Payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue absent fraud or demonstrable error.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-23","number":"23","heading":"RECORDS AND CUSTOMER ASSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24","number":"24","heading":"ASSIGNMENT AND CHANGE OF CONTROL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.1","number":"24.1","heading":"Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.3","number":"24.3","heading":"For other assignments, neither Party may assign without the other's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. A permitted assignment does not relieve accrued obligations. An attempted assignment contrary to this Section is void to the extent permitted by law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-24.4","number":"24.4","heading":"Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service. Vendor shall maintain accurate books and promptly report a credible suspected violation materially related to the Services.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.3","number":"26.3","heading":"Each Party shall comply with applicable export-control and sanctions laws. Vendor is responsible for classifying Vendor Technology and identifying restrictions before delivery. Customer will not knowingly permit access from a comprehensively sanctioned jurisdiction contrary to written notice and Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-26.4","number":"26.4","heading":"Vendor shall comply with reasonable Customer workplace, safety, security, and acceptable-use policies supplied in advance while accessing Customer facilities or systems. A policy does not amend commercial terms or impose obligations unrelated to that access.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27","number":"27","heading":"FORCE MAJEURE AND BUSINESS CONTINUITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.1","number":"27.1","heading":"Neither Party is liable for delay caused by an event beyond its reasonable control that could not have been prevented through reasonable care, excluding inability to pay, staffing shortages, subcontractor failure that could reasonably be avoided, or a cyberattack preventable by required safeguards. Plans will address redundant systems, backups, recovery objectives, communications, and alternate personnel. Vendor shall provide a current executive summary on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-27.3","number":"27.3","heading":"If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28.2","number":"28.2","heading":"The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-28.3","number":"28.3","heading":"Before filing an ordinary commercial claim, a Party shall give notice and permit executives with settlement authority to meet in good faith within fifteen business days. This process does not delay urgent relief or a filing needed to preserve a limitations period. Discussions are compromise negotiations to the extent allowed by law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29","number":"29","heading":"NOTICES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29.1","number":"29.1","heading":"Legal notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by nationally recognized overnight courier or certified mail, return receipt requested, to the address in the preamble and by email to the legal-notice address stated in the applicable Order Form. Operational notices may be delivered through agreed service channels.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29.2","number":"29.2","heading":"Notice is effective on documented delivery, except a refusal is deemed delivery. A Party may change its notice address by notice under this Section. Email alone is insufficient for breach, termination, indemnity, assignment, or litigation notices unless receipt is affirmatively acknowledged.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-29.3","number":"29.3","heading":"Notices to Customer must copy legal@northwind.example, and notices to Vendor must copy legal@brightline.example. Automated portal messages, invoices, and website postings are not legal notices.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30","number":"30","heading":"GENERAL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-30.1","number":"30.1","heading":"The Parties are independent contractors. You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

No liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Liquidated damages exceeding the remaining contract value or triggered by minor breaches.

Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

The licence grant in § 13 meets our preferred position on every material term:

- **§ 13.1** — subscription grant runs to Customer, "its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf," plus Authorized Users; worldwide, non-exclusive, and *not* labelled revocable or non-transferable.
- **§ 13.2** — paid-up software and Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables are licensed to Customer and its Affiliates on a "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid" basis, with modification/derivative rights and contractor support. **§ 14.3** confirms this licence reaches Vendor Technology required to use a Deliverable.
- **§ 13.3** — transfer to an Affiliate or successor is permitted via § 24 (§ 24.1 allows M&A/asset-sale assignment without consent; § 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating, suspending, or repricing on our change of control). Revocation or suspension is confined to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure opportunity — no at-will revocation anywhere in the document (checked all "suspend" occurrences).
- **§ 13.4** — restrictions are ordinary and well-qualified ("knowingly," subject to Applicable Law, with carve-outs for authorized security testing and use of Customer Data and output); they do not narrow the grant.

This sits at the preferred position, not merely the fallback, so no changes are warranted.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.comment: [Playbook] We can accommodate usage verification, but our playbook requires audits to be no more than once every twelve months on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and without access to our systems. We have also removed the remote-access right, which conflicts with Section 22.2's existing no-direct-access protection.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor, and remove remote system access.
input.comment: [Playbook] We can accommodate usage verification, but our playbook requires audits to be no more than once every twelve months on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and without access to our systems. We have also removed the remote-access right, which conflicts with Section 22.2's existing no-direct-access protection.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Redwood Commerce Group, Inc.; counterparty is Silverline Systems Ltd..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
input.rationale: Section 19 meets or exceeds the preferred position. 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty by qualified personnel plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and specifications; 19.2 runs ninety days from the later of delivery or acceptance for Deliverables and for the full subscription term for hosted Services (better than the 12-month software benchmark); 19.3 adds no-malicious-code, compliance with Applicable Law, no functionality diminution and open-source protection. 19.4 supplies the required remedy ladder — prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure in a reasonable period — and expressly preserves other remedies for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The 19.5 disclaimer is mutual and expressly does not limit any express warranty, so it does not swallow the warranty. No redline needed.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule: RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window

Preferred position:
Renewal only by mutual written agreement; or automatic 12-month renewals that Customer may opt out of on 30 days' notice, with a Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal; price increases capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 %.


Fallback position:
Automatic renewal with a non-renewal notice window of no more than 60 days; price increases ≤ 5 %.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

Rendered redlined clause:
8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives 30 days' advance written notice.
Vendor will notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the renewal date.
8.3 On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.

Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Redwood Commerce Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Silverline Systems Ltd., a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Order Form: 1.6 “Order Form” means a written ordering document signed by authorized representatives of both Parties that references this Agreement and describes the Services, Deliverables, subscription quantities, service levels, Fees, and term purchased by Customer. A purchase order is an administrative convenience only and does not amend an Order Form or this Agreement.

Acceptance remedies in 6.2 (correction cycles, then termination and refund) reinforce rather than displace this. Nothing here needs to be traded for.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 grants unlimited, unannounced audits plus remote access to our systems — squarely within the rule's walk-away territory and failing the fallback on frequency, notice and system access. Sections 22.2 and 22.3 are protective (Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds five percent, no direct system access, findings are our Confidential Information) and meet the preferred cost position, but they do not cure 22.1 and in fact conflict with its remote-access grant. We therefore redline 22.1 only, to once per twelve months on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, with no system access; cost allocation is left to 22.2.

proposal.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor, and remove remote system access.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accommodate usage verification, but our playbook requires audits to be no more than once every twelve months on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and without access to our systems. We have also removed the remote-access right, which conflicts with Section 22.2's existing no-direct-access protection.

ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours and without unreasonably disrupting Customer's operations. Each audit shall be conducted by an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, and Vendor and its auditor shall have no remote or direct access to Customer's systems; Customer will instead provide relevant usage records.

Vendor shall keep accurate action and decision logs and furnish them to Customer on request.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6","number":"6","heading":"ACCEPTANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.1","number":"6.1","heading":"Customer will have fifteen business days after delivery of a Deliverable to test it against the acceptance criteria in the applicable Order Form. Customer may accept it in writing or reject it by describing material nonconformities. Payment, productive use needed for testing, or silence does not constitute acceptance.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-6.2","number":"6.2","heading":"If Customer rejects a Deliverable, Vendor shall promptly correct the nonconformities at no additional charge and resubmit it for a new acceptance period. After two unsuccessful correction cycles, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of Fees paid for the rejected Deliverable and dependent Services Customer cannot reasonably use.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7","number":"7","heading":"FEES, INVOICING, AND TAXES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.1","number":"7.1","heading":"Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2","number":"7.2","heading":"Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.2-2","number":"7.2","heading":"Vendor shall invoice no more frequently than monthly in arrears, except that an Order Form may state annual subscription Fees are invoiced in advance. Each invoice must identify the Order Form, period, Services, quantities, applicable credits, and a valid purchase-order number if Customer supplied one. Proper undisputed invoices are due forty-five days after receipt.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.3","number":"7.3","heading":"Customer may withhold a genuinely disputed amount by notifying Vendor before its due date and explaining the basis. The Parties will work promptly and in good faith to resolve the dispute. Vendor shall continue the Services while a payment dispute is pending and shall not charge interest on an amount ultimately found not due.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.4","number":"7.4","heading":"Fees exclude sales, use, value-added, and similar transaction taxes that Vendor is legally required to collect and separately states on a valid invoice. Customer is not responsible for taxes on Vendor's income, property, payroll, personnel, or franchise, or for taxes avoidable through Vendor's timely use of a valid exemption certificate.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.5","number":"7.5","heading":"Pre-approved travel expenses are reimbursable at cost without markup and in accordance with Customer's travel policy. Vendor shall provide receipts and request reimbursement within sixty days. All other expenses are included in the Fees.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-7.6","number":"7.6","heading":"Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8","number":"8","heading":"TERM AND RENEWAL","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.1","number":"8.1","heading":"This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for three years unless earlier terminated in accordance with its terms. Expiration of this Agreement does not itself terminate an Order Form then in effect; this Agreement continues to govern that Order Form until the Order Form expires or is terminated.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.2","number":"8.2","heading":"Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-8.3","number":"8.3","heading":"On renewal, Vendor may increase recurring Fees only by the lesser of the increase in the United States Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers during the preceding twelve months and three percent. Vendor must give at least ninety days' written notice of an increase. No increase applies to prepaid periods.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9","number":"9","heading":"TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.1","number":"9.1","heading":"Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail. If a breach cannot reasonably be cured within thirty days, the cure period extends up to sixty additional days while the breaching Party diligently pursues cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.2","number":"9.2","heading":"Either Party may terminate immediately by written notice if the other becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for creditors, enters liquidation, or becomes subject to a bankruptcy proceeding not dismissed within sixty days. A lawful reorganization that does not impair performance is not, by itself, grounds for termination.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.3","number":"9.3","heading":"Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-9.5","number":"9.5","heading":"Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10","number":"10","heading":"EFFECT OF EXPIRY OR TERMINATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.1","number":"10.1","heading":"On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-10.2","number":"10.2","heading":"Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11","number":"11","heading":"TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND DATA RETURN","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.1","number":"11.1","heading":"Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.2","number":"11.2","heading":"Within thirty days after Customer's request, Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use. Vendor shall not withhold Customer Data because of a fee dispute.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-11.3","number":"11.3","heading":"After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. Any retained copy remains protected and may not be used for another purpose.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12","number":"12","heading":"CUSTOMER RESPONSIBILITIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-12.3","number":"12.3","heading":"Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.2","number":"13.2","heading":"For software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.3","number":"13.3","heading":"Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24. Vendor shall not revoke or suspend a licence except during a material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-13.4","number":"13.4","heading":"Customer shall not knowingly reverse engineer hosted source code except to the extent a restriction is prohibited by Applicable Law, interfere with the Services, bypass documented security controls, or use the Services to violate Applicable Law. These restrictions do not limit testing authorized by the security exhibit or use of Customer Data and output.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14","number":"14","heading":"INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND DELIVERABLES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.1","number":"14.1","heading":"As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. Vendor will execute further documents reasonably needed to confirm ownership.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.3","number":"14.3","heading":"Vendor retains Vendor Technology. Vendor shall identify material Vendor Technology in a Deliverable before delivery and may not incorporate third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use without written approval.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-14.4","number":"14.4","heading":"No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights. Vendor is a processor or service provider and shall assist Customer with data-subject requests, impact assessments, consultations, and regulatory inquiries.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16","number":"16","heading":"CONFIDENTIALITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.1","number":"16.1","heading":"“Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.2","number":"16.2","heading":"The recipient shall use Confidential Information only to perform or exercise rights under this Agreement, protect it with at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel, Affiliates, advisers, and subcontractors who need to know and are bound by confidentiality obligations. The recipient is responsible for their unauthorized use or disclosure.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-16.5","number":"16.5","heading":"On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17","number":"17","heading":"INFORMATION SECURITY","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-17.1","number":"17.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain a written information-security program using administrative, technical, organizational, and physical safeguards appropriate to the sensitivity of Customer Data and risk. Notice will include known facts, affected data and systems, containment, and a contact.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18","number":"18","heading":"INSURANCE","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.1","number":"18.1","heading":"Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense throughout the term and for one year afterward, commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-18.2","number":"18.2","heading":"Policies will be issued by reputable insurers and be primary to Customer's insurance where commercially customary. Vendor shall give advance notice of cancellation or material reduction to the extent available from its insurer. Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor will not materially diminish functionality during a term or use open-source software in a way that requires disclosure or licensing of Customer source code.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.4","number":"19.4","heading":"For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. No disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty, or remedy expressly provided here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20","number":"20","heading":"INDEMNIFICATION","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.1","number":"20.1","heading":"Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.2","number":"20.2","heading":"Vendor shall also defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the Customer indemnified parties from third-party claims to the extent arising from Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; bodily injury, death, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.3","number":"20.3","heading":"Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor from a third-party claim alleging that unmodified Customer material supplied by Customer and used by Vendor strictly as authorized infringes an intellectual property right, or arising from Customer's violation of Applicable Law in its authorized use of the Services. (CUSTOMER)","level":1,"paragraphCount":2},{"id":"sec-p0132","heading":"SILVERLINE SYSTEMS LTD. (VENDOR)","level":1,"paragraphCount":2}]

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.

Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages payable by us (Customer) to Vendor at USD 25,000 per day for "any delay in providing a dependency" — no materiality threshold, no notice or cure period, and no aggregate cap. This fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and also fails the fallback, which tolerates only an early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount; this is a per-day penalty untethered to termination. It is close to walk-away territory because an accumulating daily amount triggered by minor delays can exceed remaining contract value, and the mutual cap in § 21.1 gives limited comfort (it is set at the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, i.e. potentially well above annual spend, and the § 7.3 withholding right covers disputed Fees rather than damages claims). We propose deleting the clause, offering day-for-day schedule relief instead.

proposal.summary: Delete the USD 25,000/day liquidated damages payable by Customer for dependency delays
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages against us: our playbook does not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Customer, and this one is uncapped, applies to any delay however minor, and carries no notice or cure period. If Vendor needs protection for dependency delays, we can instead agree a day-for-day extension of affected timelines and relief from related Vendor service commitments.
