Rule: AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer

Preferred position:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.


Fallback position:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

Drafter's locked target level: preferred

Original clause:
22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

Rendered redlined clause:
22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours and without unreasonably disrupting Customer's operations. Each audit shall be conducted by an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, and Vendor and its auditor shall have no remote or direct access to Customer's systems; Customer will instead provide relevant usage records.
22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) at § 7.6 / p0032.**

- **Issue:** § 7.6 makes us pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as "agreed liquidated damages" for *any* dependency delay — no materiality threshold, no notice/cure, no aggregate cap.
- **Why it fails:** The preferred position bars Customer-payable liquidated damages entirely; the fallback tolerates only an early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees. A per-day accruing penalty is neither, and can approach walk-away territory as it compounds.
- **Cross-checks:** § 21.1's mutual cap is the *greater* of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, so it offers little practical restraint; § 7.3's withholding right applies to disputed Fees, not damages claims, so it does not mitigate.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** delete p0032, with an offer in the comment to substitute day-for-day schedule relief for Vendor instead.

system.text:
You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

Category: transition
Position — preferred:

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19","number":"19","heading":"WARRANTIES","level":1,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.1","number":"19.1","heading":"Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.2","number":"19.2","heading":"For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.3","number":"19.3","heading":"Vendor warrants the Services and Deliverables will not contain malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, and that Vendor will comply with Applicable Law. This remedy is not exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security, or indemnified claims.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-19.5","number":"19.5","heading":"Except for the express warranties in this Agreement, neither Party makes an implied warranty to the maximum extent lawful. Customer has no obligation to the extent a claim arises from Vendor Technology, modification, combination, or instructions.","level":2,"paragraphCount":1},{"id":"sec-20.4","number":"20.4","heading":"The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, and control of the defence, except delay excuses obligations only to the extent of material prejudice. input.rationale: Section 11 contains a full exit package that meets the preferred position: 11.1 gives up to six months' transition assistance on any expiry or termination at the expiring Order Form rates (better for us than "then-current rates"), including knowledge transfer, migration and cooperation with a replacement supplier; 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, documented, machine-readable format and bars withholding data over a fee dispute; and 11.3 requires secure deletion after confirmed return with written officer certification, with any legally retained copy remaining protected. system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

This is a bounded short-document repair and you have no tools. The user supplies the exact source paragraphs, definitions, current proposal, and deterministic feedback. Return only the requested structured proposal and one-to-one element coverage. Copy every replace.oldText byte-for-byte from a supplied paragraph. Do not invent an anchor or source text.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

system.text:
You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

You are an independent contract-redline evaluator in a fresh context.
Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. First decompose the supplied preferred prose and fallback prose yourself into complete, non-overlapping atomic operative requirements. Split conjunctions when each noun, duty, remedy, duration, trigger, scope, party direction, or permitted alternative can fail independently. Evaluate both levels and quote concise evidence for every element.

A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. A governing law and forum must be a permitted corresponding pair. "Professional and workmanlike" supplies two required standards; software/documentation conformance and its period must be express. Deliverables, work product, pre-existing IP, generic tools, know-how, use, modification, and sublicensing are distinct concepts.

Minimal means no more is changed than needed to complete the selected level. Fail it for extra words, a requirement from the other level, a broad new exception, duplicated protection, unnecessary model-language boilerplate, or a whole-clause rewrite where an operator, number, or short phrase suffices. A concise insertion for an absent clause can be minimal. Quote each offending extra word or phrase exactly in offending_extra_words; use an empty list when there is none. Preserves intent means every unrelated commercial term and untouched sentence remains effective and no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Conditional requirements are met when the condition is demonstrably absent. In particular, a limitation on Customer indemnity does not require creating a Customer indemnity, and a cap on renewal price increases does not require inventing a price increase. Do not infer omitted operative language from commercial context.

Be strict about the recurring boundaries: a future Customer consent is not a present Vendor data licence; a fallback IP licence does not require a new Customer-Data processing clause; a request condition must not swallow mandatory post-termination data return; deletion and certification follow return; a fallback warranty does not permit "material" documentation conformance when the position says conformance; and a fallback numeric threshold should not be exceeded with a preferred-only amount. Return actionable reasons and exact textual evidence.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You repair the operative language of one already-detected customer-side contract finding.
Detection is locked: never change deviation to missing, compliant, or needs_review, and never change missing to another status. Work only on proposal quality.

Commit to exactly one target level. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains. Meet every atomic requirement of the selected level and add nothing solely required by the other level. Never submit a hybrid. You may replace the current target with the other complete level when a deterministic official check cannot pass the current one; switch the whole proposal, not individual elements. Where the prose uses an exact amount, basis, temporal anchor, party direction, or operative noun, put those same words in the contract: for example, "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim", "equal to 12 months' fees", "then-current rates", and "standard machine-readable format". Do not rely on the margin comment.

Treat the supplied target checklist as both floor and ceiling. Map every selected element exactly once. Use already_met only for a verbatim quote in a cited paragraph. Use addressed_by_operation only when the indexed operation actually supplies that element. A conditional requirement such as limiting Customer indemnity applies only if such an indemnity exists; do not create a new obligation merely to limit it.

Draft the smallest operative change. Change an operator, number, noun phrase, or single element cluster instead of rewriting a sentence or clause. Keep every untouched sentence and every unrelated word byte-for-byte. Never pad an anchor with a neighbouring sentence, re-condition a compound obligation, add a broad notwithstanding clause, or replace a prohibition with a duplicative catalogue of affirmative rights. If a clause is genuinely absent, use one concise insert_after clause carrying only the chosen level. Anchor a new numbered heading after the final body paragraph of the preceding section, never after the next section's heading. The pre-submit tool strictly enforces the official 0.600 changed-character ratio for each replacement; include only enough unchanged context within the same sentence to make the word-level tracked change intelligible.

Minimality is substantive as well as mechanical. Remove non-target boilerplate and broad exceptions. Do not add defence duties, hold-harmless language, settlement procedure, at-own-expense language, survival tails, extra damages categories, illustrative data categories, service standards, or remedies unless the chosen prose requires them. Preserve favourable existing language. Never grant Vendor a new right while fixing a Customer right.

Use digit-first durations required by literal checks: "60 days' notice" and "90 days", not "sixty (60) days". When a deterministic check requires the generic represented-party label, make "Customer may terminate" operative without changing who the defined customer is. Re-read the returned official-check failures and repair their literal cause.

Rule-specific precision:
- LOL-CAP: fallback means a cap equal to 12 months' fees, with no USD floor. Preferred requires the operative lowercase words "fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim"—never capital-F Fees when that defined term is narrow and never an event anchor—plus the USD 1M limb, every preferred carve-out, and a statement that all Customer payment obligations are not damages.
- INDEMN: preferred means Vendor defends and indemnifies only Customer and affiliates. Do not add hold-harmless language, officers, directors, employees, agents, a Customer defence duty, settlement mechanics, separate counsel, admissions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, or other fallback/customary extras. For a one-sided clause, a short fallback Vendor IP indemnity insertion with only the stated exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap is often more minimal than rewriting Customer's clause.
- GOVLAW: law and forum must be one permitted corresponding pair. Cure every conflicting retained law or forum, including an injunction carve-out permitting proceedings in any or another court; limit relief to the designated courts using a small same-sentence edit.
- IP: distinguish deliverables from work product and pre-existing Vendor IP from generic tools and know-how. Preferred must license any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables but must not add fallback-only worldwide, modification, or sublicensing rights or ownership of Customer Content/Marks beyond the required Customer Data protection. Do not add a Customer-Data processing restriction to a fallback licence because that requirement is absent from the fallback prose. When rewriting ownership would exceed 0.600, choose the shorter fallback and use a concise insert_after that states Vendor's generic-tools and know-how ownership and makes Customer's Deliverables licence perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and usable, modifiable, and sublicensable for its business. If the source licence has contrary limitations, disapply only those exact limitations in the preceding sentence; do not use a broad notwithstanding clause.
- INSURANCE: add only the listed policies, limits, Customer-Data condition, workers' compensation, and certificate right. Never add a post-termination coverage or survival tail.
- LICENSE: prefer the two-element fallback when affiliate coverage on written notice and a Customer M&A-successor transfer cure the deviation. Grant the successor right only to Customer, not Vendor or either Party generally. At fallback, do not add contractors, paid-up/perpetual/irrevocable rights, subscription protections, or general successor rights.
- WARRANTY: state professional and workmanlike performance separately and make software conformance to documentation express. Use only repair, replacement, and refund—never re-performance. Use the exact 90-day fallback software period and 30-day Services period unless completing every preferred element.
- RENEWAL: an automatic-renewal proposal must state a renewal-price cap even when the original is silent: lesser of CPI and 3% for preferred, exactly 5% for fallback. Use the exact notice form a deterministic check can read.
- EXCLUSIVITY: fallback's defined product category cannot retain "substantially similar", "companies similar", "including without limitation", or another open-ended analogue. Delete that vague scope while adding the 12-month and performance exits.
- NOSOLICIT: use the complete fallback because the official literal checks require a 12-month period and a general-solicitation carve-out. Make it mutual, limit it to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months from the end of involvement, carve out general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and remove every no-hire restriction. A reliable low-ratio construction is to replace the existing sentence with "Customer shall not solicit any Vendor personnel during the term or for 12 months after the end of their involvement in the Services", then insert one concise sentence making the same scope mutual and expressly limiting the preceding sentence to personnel directly involved in the Services, with both carve-outs. Preserve any numbering and enough unchanged source words to keep the replacement at or below 0.600.
- LD: fallback applies only to an early-termination fee; do not leave a payment triggered by termination generally. State the three-month cap and that it is the sole liquidated amount.
- TRANSITION: do not place all duties behind "at Customer's request". State the duration, then-current rates, data return/export, 30-day deadline, standard machine-readable format, deletion, and certification required by the chosen level, with deletion after return.
- MINCOMMIT: never delete the paragraph. Retain its existing sentence and minimally change the amount and take-or-pay mechanic so Customer commits to "no minimum amount" and "pays only for Services ordered or used"; this preserves the anchor while eliminating both commitment and take-or-pay. Keep unchanged scaffolding such as "Customer commits to purchase ... of Services in each ... on a ... basis" where present—the goal is an operative cure whose replacement ratio is just under 0.600, not a polished whole-sentence rewrite.
- Other absence positions such as NONCOMPETE, MFN, and LD are usually cured most minimally by changing the prohibitory or mandatory operator while leaving the negated mechanics intact; do not restate protections already present elsewhere.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be verbatim from the supplied source. Comments begin with the playbook prefix and explain only the operative change.

This is a bounded short-document repair and you have no tools. The user supplies the exact source paragraphs, definitions, current proposal, and deterministic feedback. Return only the requested structured proposal and one-to-one element coverage. Copy every replace.oldText byte-for-byte from a supplied paragraph. Do not invent an anchor or source text.

Evaluate operative language, never promises in the margin comment or the drafter's checklist. A level is complete only when all of its atomic elements are met. Preferred and fallback are separate bargains: do not combine selected pieces from each. Read exact words literally. A cap "equal to 12 months' fees" is not met by a greater-of cap. "Fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim" is not met by all amounts, paid-only fees, the first order, or a period preceding an event. Fallback position:
Mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches; no "no-hire".

Preferred position:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.


Fallback position:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.

22.2 Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-27af6fdd","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.","rationale":"Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims arising from the Services or Deliverables (20.1), and for Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2). Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material and Customer's violation of law in authorized use), with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. Standard procedure (prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, settlement-consent protections) appears in 20.4, and the infringement remedies (procure, modify/replace, refund) in 20.5, with a matching termination right in 9.3. Notably, indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so Vendor's indemnity is not subject to the general cap or to a super-cap — better than the fallback and favourable to us. No redline warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-9dea1dac","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","rationale":"Section 14 meets our preferred position in full. 14.1 confirms Customer owns Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information and Customer pre-existing IP, with no transfer to Vendor beyond a limited processing right (reinforced by 15.1's no-sale/no-model-training restriction). 14.2 vests ownership of Deliverables in Customer on creation with a present assignment from Vendor and personnel-level assignments. 14.3 leaves Vendor Technology with Vendor (acceptable) but applies the Section 13.2 perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to any Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable, including modification and contractor support. 14.4 excludes joint ownership absent a signed instrument and preserves Customer's unrestricted rights in its own feedback. No walk-away triggers (no assignment of Customer IP/Data, no joint ownership, no vendor-owned deliverables without licence back). Minor note only, not a deviation: the 13.2 licence lists contractor support rather than an express sublicensing right, which is immaterial given Customer owns the Deliverables outright.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-85b7fb6d","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21 meets the preferred position. The cap in 21.1 is expressly mutual and set at the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve months preceding the claim event and (b) USD 1,000,000. \"Fees\" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is meaningful rather than illusory. Section 21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and helpfully confirms that data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages. Section 21.3 places outside the cap each Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not \"damages\" subject to the cap — the latter is a benefit to neither side unfairly and mirrors our model language. Section 21.4 preserves independence of each cap/exclusion and survival of failure of essential purpose, and §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No one-sided cap, no indemnities inside the cap. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-506eac42","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets our preferred position on every material term. 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free affiliate/successor (M&A and asset-sale) carve-out, subject only to prompt notice and assignee assumption. 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance and change-of-control transfers to Customer's prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld for a capable, financially sound assignee) and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service on Customer's change of control. 24.3's catch-all is expressly limited to \"other assignments\" and so does not undercut the 24.1 carve-out, and 13.3 carries the licence rights across a permitted assignment. No Vendor exit or re-pricing trigger appears elsewhere in the document (9.2 is an ordinary insolvency clause that expressly excludes lawful reorganizations). No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-d350eef7","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.","rationale":"Section 2.2 binds Customer to use Vendor as its sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the entire three-year term, with no category limitation, no 12-month cap, and no performance-based exit. That is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback on every material term. It also conflicts directly with Section 2.1 (no minimum quantity or purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment), so deletion both meets the preferred position and resolves the internal inconsistency. Exclusivity running in our favour (e.g., the non-exclusive licence in 13.1) is unaffected.","proposal":"Convert 2.2 sole-and-exclusive provider commitment to non-exclusive","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-license-549eeb36","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","rationale":"Section 13 satisfies the preferred position in full. 13.1 extends the subscription grant to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on their behalf (plus Authorized Users), with no \"revocable\" or \"non-transferable\" language. 13.2 grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence for paid-up software and Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables, including contractor support; 14.3 confirms that licence covers Vendor Technology required to use a Deliverable. 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor under Section 24 (24.1 allows M&A/asset-sale assignment without consent; 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or suspending on our change of control) and limits revocation or suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a reasonable cure period, so the licence is not revocable at will. 13.4's use restrictions are ordinary and qualified (\"knowingly\", subject to Applicable Law, with carve-outs for authorized security testing and Customer Data/output) and do not cut back the grant. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-f6f22fb5","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"§ 12.3 expressly preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, license, sell or use any product or service and to operate in any field or territory, and records that we have given no non-compete or field-of-use commitment. This meets the preferred position (no non-compete restriction on Customer). No other clause binds us competitively: § 2.1 confirms no purchase commitment, § 13.4 is a standard acceptable-use restriction rather than a competitive covenant, and § 24.2 restricts Vendor, not us. § 2.2 (sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services) is a supply-exclusivity term that sits under the separate exclusivity rule and is addressed there rather than double-flagged here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-26d881b7","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.","rationale":"Section 28.1 selects New York law (with CISG excluded) and 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County, with each Party submitting to personal jurisdiction and waiving venue/forum objections. That matches our preferred position exactly. No arbitration provision exists anywhere in the document, so there is no foreign seat concern. The carve-out permitting temporary injunctive relief elsewhere and the 28.3 executive escalation (which expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings) are mutual and do not displace the New York courts. Compliant at the preferred position; no redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-9508e255","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 This Agreement establishes the legal terms under which Customer and its Affiliates may purchase Services from Vendor. No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.","rationale":"The Agreement meets our preferred position: § 2.1 (p0012) expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms that declining a further Order Form is neither a breach nor a shortfall, so fees are payable only for Services actually ordered. § 7.1 (p0026) reinforces this by barring any minimum-use or similar charge not identified in an Order Form, and § 12.3 (p0050) records that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. No take-or-pay, volume floor, or shortfall penalty is imposed on us anywhere in the document; the only \"shortfall\" references (§§ 22.2–22.3) concern audit underpayments for usage actually consumed, which is not a purchase commitment. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-0d12d799","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.","rationale":"Section 12.4 binds only the Customer, runs eighteen months from termination (not from the end of a person's involvement), covers every person employed by Vendor at any time during the term rather than only personnel directly involved in the Services, bars \"engage\" as well as solicit (a de facto no-hire), and contains no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. That fails the fallback on every material term (mutuality, scope, duration trigger, carve-outs, no no-hire). Section 12.3's general-recruitment language sits in tension with it but does not cure the defect, since 12.4 still bars engaging Vendor personnel however sourced. Following the rule's redline guidance we narrowed to the fallback rather than deleting outright: mutual, solicitation-only, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, twelve months from the end of that involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.","proposal":"Cut no-hire wording, set 12 months from end of involvement, and add a mutual, directly-involved-only sentence with both carve-outs","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-renewal-1a3830ee","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.","rationale":"Order Forms auto-renew for twelve months (acceptable term length) and § 8.3 already caps uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice, which meets our preferred pricing position and is not flagged. However, the non-renewal notice window is 180 days, well beyond the 60-day fallback and past the 90-day walk-away threshold, so exit is impractical. Redline shortens the window to 30 days and adds a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder to reach the preferred position; 60 days remains an acceptable fallback.","proposal":"Cut non-renewal notice to 30 days and add a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-transition-8d62b42e","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer-side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement (Vendor: Silverline)

---

## Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The core ri[REDACTED] architecture is strong and, in several respects, better than our preferred position: indemnification (§ 20), IP and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), limitation of liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), warranties (§ 19), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), insurance (§ 18), and governing law/venue (§ 28) are all compliant. Notably, indemnification obligations sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims (§ 21.3), and the cap itself is mutual at the greater of twelve months' Fees and USD 1,000,000.

The problems are concentrated in a cluster of Customer-burdening commercial terms that are inconsistent with the balance of the document and, in several cases, with each other. Six items require change:

- **Exclusivity (§ 2.2)** — a three-year sole-and-exclusive supply commitment binding us, which directly contradicts § 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (no exclusivity commitment).
- **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.6)** — USD 25,000 per day for any delay in providing a dependency, uncapped and with no materiality threshold or cure period.
- **Most-favoured-nation obligation running against us (§ 7.2)** — unlimited in scope and duration, and contradicted by § 12.3.
- **Vendor audit rights (§ 22.1)** — unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems.
- **Non-solicitation (§ 12.4)** — one-way, eighteen-month, de facto no-hire covering all Vendor personnel.
- **Non-renewal notice (§ 8.2)** — 180 days, which is past our walk-away threshold and makes exit impractical.
- **Termination for convenience** — absent entirely for a three-year term (§ 9 is for-cause only).

Four of the internally inconsistent clauses (§§ 2.2, 7.2, 7.6, 8.2) should be straightforward to resolve because the Agreement's own provisions already disclaim the commitments they impose. Two redlines (§ 12.4 and § 22.1) did not verify cleanly and require drafting attention before the turn goes out.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with §§ 20.2–20.5, 9.3, 21.3) | Preferred position in full; indemnities are Excluded Claims outside the cap. |
| Critical | Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with §§ 14.2–14.4, 13.2, 15.1) | Preferred position; Deliverables vest in Customer on creation. |
| Critical | Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees or USD 1,000,000; full carve-outs. |
| High | Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Consent-free affiliate/successor carve-out; no Vendor repricing on our change of control. |
| **High** | **Exclusivity obligations binding Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 2.2** | **Three-year sole-and-exclusive supply commitment; no category limit, no cap, no performance exit. Walk-away territory; conflicts with §§ 2.1 and 12.3.** |
| High | Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.4, 14.3, 24.1, 24.4) | Extends to Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users; not revocable at will. |
| High | Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | Expressly preserves our commercial freedom; § 2.2 addressed under the exclusivity rule. |
| Medium | Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) | New York law and New York County courts; CISG excluded; no arbitration clause. |
| Medium | Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with §§ 7.1, 12.3) | No minimum quantity, volume floor or shortfall penalty. |
| **Medium** | **Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 12.4** | **One-way, 18 months post-termination, all Vendor personnel, "engage" as well as solicit, no carve-outs. Fails fallback on every material term. Redline did not verify.** |
| **Medium** | **Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window** | **Deviation** | **§ 8.2** | **180-day non-renewal notice, past the 90-day walk-away threshold. Uplift cap in § 8.3 already meets our preferred position and is not flagged.** |
| Medium | Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with §§ 11.2–11.3, 16.5) | Six months' assistance at expiring Order Form rates; data return in 30 days; no data-hostage right. |
| Medium | Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) | Meets or exceeds preferred position, including remedy ladder and mutual disclaimer. |
| **Low** | **Audit rights against Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 22.1** | **Unlimited, unannounced audits plus remote system access — walk-away territory. §§ 22.2–22.3 are protective but do not cure § 22.1. Redline did not verify.** |
| Low | Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) | CGL, E&O and cyber limits all at preferred position; insurance does not limit liability. |
| **Low** | **Liquidated damages payable by Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 7.6** | **USD 25,000/day for any dependency delay; no materiality threshold, notice, cure or aggregate cap. Fails preferred and fallback positions.** |
| **Low** | **Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer** | **Deviation** | **§ 7.2** | **Unlimited MFN running against us, no scope, duration or comparison carve-outs. Walk-away territory; conflicts with § 12.3.** |
| **Low** | **Termination for convenience** | **Missing** | § 9.3 (for-cause only; §§ 9.1–9.2, 8.2, 27.3 do not supply a convenience right) | **No Customer right to terminate without cause in a three-year term. Walk-away territory.** |

---

## Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **§ 2.2 — Exclusivity.** A three-year sole-and-exclusive supply commitment with no category limitation, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit. Our position is non-exclusivity; deletion also resolves the direct conflict with §§ 2.1 and 12.3.
2. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** Unlimited in scope, duration and product, with no comparison carve-outs. Our position is no MFN burden on Customer. § 12.3 already records that we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
3. **§ 22.1 — Vendor audit rights.** Audits at any time without notice, with remote access to our systems. Our position is once per twelve months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, no system access; cost allocation can remain with § 22.2.
4. **Termination for convenience (absent).** No provision permits us to exit without cause during the three-year term. Our position is 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, keyed to § 10.2, inserted as a new § 9.4.
5. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice.** Past the 90-day walk-away threshold; exit is impractical as drafted. We seek 30 days plus a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder; 60 days remains an acceptable fallback.
6. **§ 7.6 — Daily liquidated damages against us.** Close to walk-away: an accumulating uncapped daily amount triggered by any dependency delay can exceed remaining contract value, and the mutual cap in § 21.1 gives limited comfort because it is set at the *greater* of twelve months' Fees and USD 1,000,000.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the first turn on the four verified redlines.** §§ 2.2 (non-exclusive), 7.2 (negate the Customer-side MFN), 7.6 (remove the USD 25,000/day charge, offering day-for-day schedule relief instead) and 8.2 (30-day non-renewal notice plus 60-day Vendor reminder) are drafted and verified. In each case we should lead with the internal inconsistency — §§ 2.1, 7.1 and 12.3 already disclaim the very commitments these clauses impose — which should make these low-friction asks.
2. **Re-draft the two unverified redlines before they leave the building.** The § 12.4 non-solicitation redline (mutual, solicitation-only, personnel directly involved in the Services, twelve months from the end of that involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs) and the § 22.1 audit redline (once per twelve months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site, independent auditor, no system access) both failed verification and need a further drafting pass.
3. **Insert the new § 9.4 termination-for-convenience clause.** 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees keyed to § 10.2. The section number 9.4 is currently unused. Note for the business: Vendor has no convenience right either, so only the Customer-side gap needs closing — we should resist any reciprocal Vendor exit right offered in exchange.
4. **Confirm the commercial position on exclusivity with the business owner.** If Vendor pushes back on § 2.2, we need to know whether any exclusivity was in fact negotiated, given § 12.3 states the opposite.
5. **Hold the compliant provisions.** §§ 11, 13, 14, 18, 19, 20, 21, 24 and 28 meet or exceed our positions. We should avoid reopening them and, in particular, protect the Excluded Claims list in § 21.3 and the six-month transition package in § 11.1 if Vendor seeks trade-offs for the changes above.

*Minor points noted for the record but not redlined: the § 13.2 licence lists contractor support rather than an express sublicensing right (immaterial given we own the Deliverables outright).*"}
